content: Most individuals infected with Human Herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) will remain asymptomatic. It is currently unknown whether treating asymptomatic patients can reduce the likelihood of subsequent infections. In immunocompetent individuals who present with uncomplicated skin manifestations associated with HHV-7, such as roseola infantum or pityriasis rosea, only symptomatic management is required. For patients who are HIV-positive, initiating antiretroviral therapy may be recommended. There are no established clinical scenarios that specifically necessitate antiviral therapy for HHV-7. The most effective antiviral agents against HHV-7 are cidofovir and foscarnet.
